newsitem.title: USA: China delays TCK smut discussions--USDA.
newsitem.headline: China delays TCK smut discussions--USDA.

text.p: China has postponed a visit planned for next week to discuss the TCK smut dispute that has effectively shut down U.S. wheat sales to Beijing, an Agriculture Department official said Friday.

Paul Drazek, the department's trade adviser, said China announced the decision overnight due to "technical scheduling problems." Officials will try to set a new date for the visit in the next few weeks.
In a speech at a grain conference, Drazek also expressed disppointment at new steps by the European Union to subsidize its grain exports.
USDA will assess grain market factors, including U.S. competitiveness, before deciding whether to retaliate with its own export subsidies, Drazek said.
The Chinese delegation had been scheduled to begin its visit on Monday with visits to U.S. wheat-growing regions at port facilities before travelling to Washington for USDA consultations.
Officials from China's plant quarantine and grain buying agencies were to be among the delegation.
China has refused to accept U.S. wheat unless it was guaranteed free of TCK smut.
